correctness.rationale: Every codimension-three quotient of a two-step nilpotent Lie algebra is either abelian or Heisenberg over any finite field. Surjective Lie maps to Heisenberg are determined by vector assignments satisfying nonedge determinant-zero constraints and free central lifts. Support components in the complement graph carry projective lines; spanning assignments require at least two distinct lines. The explicit empty-support correction and division by q²|GL₂(q)| yield a complete kernel count. A separate exhaustive reduced-row-echelon ideal test matches 21 finite configurations; the unrestricted proof does not depend on finite tests.

originality.rationale: An unrestricted exact codimension-three ideal coefficient is established from a new Heisenberg-kernel/projective-line classification and the classical induced-subgraph component polynomial. The closest primary graph-ideal article classifies some graph-induced ideals, while general finite-field ideal-zeta methods compute ideals algorithmically without asserting this all-simple-graph closed form. Previously known star-specific ideal enumeration is acknowledged as covered and not claimed independently. No direct equivalent or stronger published theorem was found in the inspected material; undiscovered implicit equivalences remain a genuine risk.
residual_risks: A nonindexed general ideal-zeta theorem for graph-associated Lie algebras or a p-group normal-subgroup count may implicitly specialize to the same formula.
The previously obtained star-graph ideal polynomial covers the special case of stars and must not be claimed new.
A complete independent literature-priority audit has not been performed.

value.rationale: Codimensions one and two cannot detect a nonabelian nilpotent quotient, making codimension three the first naturally bracket-sensitive ideal coefficient. The result gives a new complete exact expression for all finite simple graph Lie algebras and identifies a direct connection with an established graph polynomial, facilitating computation without ideal enumeration. This is not merely a small arbitrary numerical instance or a reindexing of published star cases.
